clue.text: Animal having to evade inconsiderate driver?

parts.note: to hedge is to dodge or evade a question
a road hog is a selfish, inconsiderate motorist

explanation.surface: A creature that has to dodge a reckless motorist on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at the creature's famous fate on roads, but 'inconsiderate driver' is the road hog.
explanation.definitionFit: This spiny insect-eating mammal is a familiar small animal of British gardens.

clue.text: Unwanted surveillance by dirty Dick?

parts.note: dirty in the sense of wicked or vile
a dick is slang for a detective, also called a private eye

explanation.surface: A grubby private investigator keeping an unwelcome watch on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dick' looks like a man's name, but it is slang for a detective, whose other slang name is 'eye'.
explanation.definitionFit: A malevolent look believed to cast harm is a gaze nobody wants turned on them.

clue.text: I'm rather slow to sag with drop shot

indicators.note: shot in the sense of ruined or wrecked, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits to slowness and to slumping with a weak drop shot in tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' turns TO SAG plus DROP into a creature. The definition is spoken by the snail or slug itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails and slugs are this class of mollusc, proverbially sluggish movers.

clue.text: Bird in pursuit

explanation.surface: A pastime of chasing birds.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a small falcon; the other is a leisure pastime one pursues.

clue.text: Low-down hack

parts.note: a journalist who peddles the low-down, the inside scoop on people, could be called a disreputable hack

explanation.surface: A despicable writer for hire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low-down' reads as base or despicable, but here it means inside information about people.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper writer of tittle-tattle about celebrities supplies the inside story.

clue.text: Bird's egg found beside Scottish river around middle of March

parts.note: an egg is O for its shape

indicators.note: around tells us the river's name surrounds another letter

parts.note: the Spey is a river in the Scottish Highlands

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of the word March

explanation.surface: A bird's egg is discovered on a Scottish riverbank in mid-March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts R, the middle of 'March', inside SPEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish-eating raptor that famously nests in Scotland.

clue.text: Forces bobsleigh to crash endlessly

indicators.note: to crash suggests the letters smashing into a new order
endlessly drops the first and last letters of bobsleigh

explanation.surface: Something compels a bobsleigh to crash again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims bobsleigh to OBSLEIG, and 'to crash' rearranges those letters. 'endlessly' reads as 'repeatedly' but means 'without its ends'.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel someone to act is the verb sense of this word.

clue.text: Not a square meal?

parts.note: a square meal is a filling one, but read literally a round dish is the opposite of square

explanation.surface: A snack that does not fill you up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square meal' is an idiom for a hearty meal; the cryptic reading takes square as a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian dish is baked as a flat disc, so it is round rather than square.

clue.text: One refined electronic image with core removed

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: core removed means the central letter of the seven-letter word for image goes

parts.note: an image is a picture

explanation.surface: A refined person producing an electronic image after removing its core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with core removed' takes T, the middle letter, out of PICTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of discerning, cultivated taste in food and drink.

clue.text: Trains initially arriving in Marylebone station

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the following four words

explanation.surface: Trains arriving at a London terminus, Marylebone station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trains' is a verb, as in trains a gun. Marylebone is a London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: To train a weapon on a target is to point it.

clue.text: Working girl that has roots

parts.note: working means occupied or busy
Lizzie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A working woman with roots, maybe hair dye showing through.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a woman's hair roots, but the definition is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatiens, a popular flowering pot plant, grows from roots like any plant.

clue.text: Wearer of shiny suit in capital formerly entertaining aged uncle

indicators.note: entertaining in the sense of hosting, so one name holds the other inside it

parts.note: Peking is the former Western name for Beijing, China's capital
Edward Lear's poem begins 'O my aged Uncle Arly'

explanation.surface: A man in a glittering suit in an old capital, hosting an elderly relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' means holding inside. Uncle Arly is the old man of Edward Lear's poem. Pearly kings are London costermonger figures in suits covered in pearl buttons.
explanation.definitionFit: This Cockney charity figure wears clothes sewn with many shimmering mother-of-pearl buttons.

clue.text: Reformed drinkers without question specifying Adam's ale

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the two letters wrap round

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is the organisation of recovering drinkers

explanation.surface: Ex-drinkers, no questions asked, specify plain water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' carries its old sense of outside, not lacking. Adam's ale is an old humorous term for water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for water, used in English for water or its pale blue-green colour.

clue.text: Looks and sounds like old recorder on record?

indicators.note: sounds like signals the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Samuel Pepys was the 17th-century diarist who recorded daily life

explanation.surface: A glance at whether an old woodwind instrument sounds right on a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recorder' suggests the instrument, but means a diarist: Pepys, pronounced 'peeps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick furtive glances are the noun sense of this word.

clue.text: Ideally one tries to get six cake tiers prepared

definitions.text: Ideally one tries to get six

indicators.note: prepared in the sense of made ready, so the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone aims to make six tiers for a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges CAKE TIERS. Six (6.0) was the perfect mark under the old figure-skating scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitive skater once aimed for a perfect 6.0 from the judges.

clue.text: On which a G-string cannot be played

definitions.text: On which a G-string cannot be played

parts.words: On which a G-string cannot be played
parts.note: an imaginary instrument has no real strings, so neither the G string nor any other can be plucked

explanation.surface: A remark about something too risqué, or an instrument lacking a string.
explanation.walkthrough: 'G-string' suggests the skimpy garment; here it is a guitar string, absent on a mimed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A guitar mimed by a rock fan has only imaginary strings.

clue.text: A specifically long drink

parts.note: a long drink normally means a large glass, but this one is a long drink of a measured length

explanation.surface: A tall drink, exactly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long drink' means a tall glass of something; 'specifically' points to a drink whose glass is a stated length of three feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall trumpet-shaped glass about three feet in length, holding beer, drunk as a pub feat.

clue.text: Girl, in time, is mean

indicators.note: in tells us the name sits inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a period of time
Vera is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl, given time, turns out to be stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like stingy, but is the arithmetic average.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics the arithmetic midpoint of a set of figures is called this.

clue.text: Stirs folk in soft bouncy bedding

indicators.note: in places the people inside the jumbled word, as if in bed
bouncy suggests the letters of soft jumping around into a new order

parts.note: folk are people, men

explanation.surface: Someone stirs folk lying in soft springy bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncy' scrambles the word soft, and 'in' places the folk inside it; 'bedding' completes the picture of people tucked into a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite or stir up trouble is the main sense of this verb.

clue.text: British girl backing swimmer

indicators.note: backing means the girl's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Mae is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A British girl supports a swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like supporting, but reverses MAE to EAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish is a creature that swims.

clue.text: Unexpectedly ratable province

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters of ratable turning up in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A Canadian region surprisingly liable to tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie region of western Canada, one of its ten provinces.

clue.text: Following old 10 in the same new round

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the turned word
new round tells us the word for ten is turned around

parts.note: the same refers back to the 10, so ten again
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Sounds like a boxing card: following on, a new round starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the same' means 10 again, TEN, which 'new round' reverses to NET; 'in' puts X, the Roman ten, inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming immediately after in order is what the word means.

clue.text: Some rail at others over amount required

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the hidden letters read upwards
some means only part of the words rail at others is used

explanation.surface: A few people rail at the others about how much money is required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks LATOT from 'rail at others' and 'over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The full sum needed, adding up all the parts.

clue.text: Offensive smell secreted by mother animal? Rubbish

indicators.note: secreted by means hidden among the other pieces

parts.note: mum is mother
Jumbo was a famous elephant, and jumbo is a name for any elephant
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A mother animal giving off a foul smell from a gland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secreted' looks like a gland producing something, but means hidden between the other two pieces. Jumbo was a famous London Zoo elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaningless jargon or superstitious nonsense.

clue.text: Cat jumps endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly removes the first and last letters of the word for jumps

parts.note: bounces means jumps

explanation.surface: A cat leaping about without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' reads as 'nonstop' but strips the ends from BOUNCES.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is also called by this name.

clue.text: Asian identity for the most part rephrased?

definitions.text: Asian identity for the most part rephrased?

indicators.note: rephrased suggests the words being put another way, so the letters are reworked
for the most part keeps the larger share of identity, dropping its last three letters

explanation.surface: An Asian person's identity, mostly described in other words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' cuts IDENTITY to IDENT; 'rephrased' rearranges ASIAN + IDENT. The whole clue also defines: an Asian identity, reworded.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Indian subcontinent, as the British once called them, is Asian.

clue.text: Head back without leader of Russian revolution

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the reversed word goes around a letter
back means the word for head is reversed

parts.note: nut is slang for head

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of Russian

explanation.surface: A head returning without the leader of the Russian Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NUT into TUN, which goes round R. 'Russian revolution' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A single rotation is one turn of a wheel.

clue.text: Actor-director, quite diminutive, is penning lines

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as a pen holds animals

parts.note: wee means very small
L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines
is abbreviated as 's

explanation.surface: A small actor-director who is busy writing lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing, but means enclosing LL inside WEES. Orson Welles directed and starred in Citizen Kane.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson, of Citizen Kane, both starred in and directed films.

clue.text: Not an out-of-court settlement?

parts.note: an out-of-court settlement avoids a law court, but a tennis set settled on the court is the reverse

explanation.surface: A legal dispute that went to trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests law; read as a tennis court, a deciding game played on court is the opposite of settling out of court.
explanation.definitionFit: A special deciding game in tennis settles a set level at six games each.
